messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — after landing the prefetch-aware kernel selector patch the H100 stacks showed a regression in tight-slo workloads. p50 ~= same, p95 +9%, p99 +12%, overall token/sec down ~7%. Seen on long-context chat streams with heavy KV hit rates.
ben: ugh. is this kv-fragmentation or scheduling churn from prefetch interfering with our continuous-batcher?
elliot: initial profiling points to more fragmented KV cache lookups (more misses across slices) and more small batches draining earlier. Kernel switching also adds 200-300us jitter when a fused kernel isn't picked.
maya: exact repro: run chat-load with seq=4096, avg prompt len 480, kv-hit ~0.7, 5k rps. baseline (old selector) p99=210ms, new selector p99=235ms.
teresa: hypothesis — prefetch is causing earlier eviction of some KV shards because slice packing density changed, which increases per-token overhead and breaks batch coalescing. We should try lowering max_tokens_per_batch on H100 and A100 separately and tighten the queue wait (allow_small_slice=false for high-prio).
ben: agree. quick experiment plan: (1) reduce max_tokens_per_batch on H100 to 160k (from 240k), (2) keep A100 at 220k but reduce max_batch_items to avoid tiny batches, (3) set batch_queue_policy=prefer_fill for the affected pool, (4) disable prefetch-forced-fallback for the canary.
elliot: sounds good. small config snippet for the experiment: ```json
{"pool":"h100-pool","max_tokens_per_batch":160000,"batch_queue_policy":"prefer_fill","allow_small_slices":false}
```
maya: will run canary now on eu-west-1-h100 (1000 qps for 15m). ops-bot: starting canary deploy (canary_id=prefetch-batch-316872) :gear:
ops-bot: canary deploy complete — traffic routing at 10% to new runtime.
teresa: also add a kernel-selection flag to prefer_fused_for_long_ctx=true for H100 canary; that reduced kernel-switch latency in earlier microbenchmarks.
ben: if that helps, follow-up autoscaling tweak: raise max_batch_wait_ms to 12ms for the pool to give more time for coalescing before scheduling.
elliot: FYI I ran a microbench: fused-pref=true + max_tokens=160k gave p99 218ms (very close to baseline) and throughput recovered to -1% vs baseline. disabling fused => p99 230ms.
maya: good sign. after canary finishes I'll snapshot traces and KV hit histograms. if stable we'll push defaults for h100 and a100 pools and add notes in runbooks about prefetch+kv interaction.
ben: one more note — L4/T4 workloads with short context saw no changes; keep their max_tokens_per_batch unchanged.
teresa: thanks team. will open a short follow-up PR with the pool default changes and a checklist for regression testing (include KV hit heatmaps + slice occupancy plots). :thumbsup:
maya: copying logs to #incidents if the canary flips.
ops-bot: canary ended — metrics: p99 delta +1.5% on canary vs baseline, throughput -0.8%, no errors. rollout recommended with flags: {"h100_max_tokens":160000,"prefuse_fused_long_ctx":true,"h100_batch_wait_ms":12}.
